definitions.explanation: A style of sushi in which vinegared rice and toppings are pressed together in a rectangular wooden mold, then cut into pieces. Especially associated with the Kansai region.

examples.japanese: {押|お}し{寿司|ずし}を{作|つく}る。
{大阪|おおさか}は{押|お}し{寿司|ずし}で{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: Osaka is famous for pressed sushi.

examples.japanese: {木|き}の{型|かた}に{酢飯|すめし}と{具|ぐ}を{入|い}れて{押|お}し{寿司|ずし}を{作|つく}った。
examples.english: I made pressed sushi by putting vinegared rice and toppings into a wooden mold.

notes:
A style of sushi where vinegared rice and toppings are pressed together in a rectangular wooden mold ({押|お}し{型|がた}), then cut into pieces. Predates the more widely known {握|にぎ}り{寿司|ずし} (hand-pressed sushi) and is especially associated with the Kansai region, particularly Osaka.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {鯖|さば}の{押|お}し{寿司|ずし}: mackerel pressed sushi
- {押|お}し{寿司|ずし}の{型|かた}: pressed sushi mold
- {柿|かき}の{葉|は}{寿司|ずし}: persimmon leaf sushi (a type of pressed sushi from Nara)

CULTURAL NOTE:
{押|お}し{寿司|ずし} is one of the oldest forms of sushi in Japan. The {鯖|さば}{寿司|ずし} (mackerel sushi) of Kyoto and the {箱|はこ}{寿司|ずし} (box sushi) of Osaka are well-known regional varieties. It is also a popular {駅弁|えきべん} (station lunch box) item.

RELATED WORDS:
- {握|にぎ}り{寿司|ずし}: hand-pressed sushi — the Tokyo-style sushi most people think of
- {箱|はこ}{寿司|ずし}: box sushi — another name for pressed sushi, especially in Osaka
- {巻|ま}き{寿司|ずし}: rolled sushi — sushi rolled in seaweed
